Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 55-year-old woman with 5-day history of dry cough and continuous rhinorrhea; no current red-flag respiratory features.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 5 days of dry, frequent cough (~every 20–30 min) and constant nasal discharge (green), feels intermittently hot with chills.
- Associated symptoms: muscle aches; transient diarrhea at onset now resolved.
- Pertinent negatives: no sputum production, chest pain, dyspnea, pleurisy, hemoptysis, epistaxis, sore throat, otalgia, rash, vomiting, current diarrhea, headaches, visual changes; drinking and urination normal.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Lisinopril “200” mg (dose appears high—verbatim from patient); Lemsip sachets 2–3/day (contains paracetamol).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies; occasional hay fever.
- Social: Lives with partner and dog; office manager; occasional alcohol (“odd sherry”); smoking status not stated.
- Last diabetes blood test ~3 weeks ago, reportedly normal.
- Height 5 ft 5 in; weight 65 kg.

Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Physical examination: not performed/recorded.

Impression:
- Probable viral upper respiratory tract infection / viral bronchitis; bacterial superinfection risk slightly increased due to diabetes.

Plan:
- Supportive care: continue Lemsip but avoid any additional paracetamol-containing products.
- Cough syrup only at night if cough prevents sleep.
- Purchase thermometer; monitor temperature regularly.
- Safety-net advice: seek review if temperature ≥ 37.5–38 °C and persistent, worsening cough, development of purulent sputum, hemoptysis, epistaxis, chest pain, or shortness of breath.
- Possible need for antibiotics if deterioration or bacterial features develop.
- Ensure routine diabetes and blood pressure follow-up with own GP.
- No immediate prescriptions or investigations today.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements:
  – Vitals, smoking status, detailed medication doses/frequencies, allergies confirmation beyond “none known,” physical examination.
● Internal conflicts:
  – Lisinopril dose reported as “200 mg” (appears unusually high)—verbatim documented.
● Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; no major inaudible sections.
